subproblems.title: Inner-product determinant covectors exist for every frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let w = (w_1, …, w_n) be any family of n vectors in ℝ^P (w : Fin n → Euclid P). Then there is an n-covector β on ℝ^P, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear form β : (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (β ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n), such that for every u = (u_1, …, u_n) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n, β(u_1, …, u_n) = det(⟨u_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b}. Here (⟨u_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} is the n×n real matrix whose entry in row a and column b is the Euclidean inner product ⟨u_a, w_b⟩, i.e. Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (u a) (w b)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (w : Fin n → Euclid P), ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ u : Fin n → Euclid P, β u = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (u a) (w b))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product on ℝ^P and ‖·‖ its norm. All matrices are n×n with rows and columns indexed by Fin n. The argument does not depend on n. For n = 0 every product below is empty (= 1), n! = 1, and the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.

1. Linear row map. Define p_w : ℝ^P → ℝ^n by p_w(x) := (⟨x, w_1⟩, …, ⟨x, w_n⟩). The real inner product is linear in its first argument: ⟨x + x', w_b⟩ = ⟨x, w_b⟩ + ⟨x', w_b⟩ and ⟨c·x, w_b⟩ = c·⟨x, w_b⟩ (inner_add_left, inner_smul_left). Hence p_w is ℝ-linear.

2. The alternating map. Let D := Matrix.detRowAlternating : (ℝ^n)^n → ℝ be the determinant viewed as a function of the n rows of a matrix; it is n-linear and alternating. Put β⁰ := D.compLinearMap p_w, i.e. β⁰(u_1, …, u_n) := D(p_w(u_1), …, p_w(u_n)). Precomposing every slot of an alternating n-linear map with one fixed linear map gives an alternating n-linear map (AlternatingMap.compLinearMap). So β⁰ : (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ is alternating and n-linear. The matrix whose a-th row is p_w(u_a) has entry ⟨u_a, w_b⟩ in row a and column b. Hence, by unfolding the definitions, β⁰(u) = det(⟨u_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => ⟨u_a, w_b⟩) for every u.

3. The bound. Fix u. By the Leibniz formula det X = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin n)} sgn(σ)·Π_a X_{σ(a), a} (Matrix.det_apply), we have β⁰(u) = Σ_σ sgn(σ)·Π_a ⟨u_{σ(a)}, w_a⟩.
(i) By the triangle inequality, |sgn σ| = 1 and |Π_a t_a| = Π_a |t_a|: |β⁰(u)| ≤ Σ_σ Π_a |⟨u_{σ(a)}, w_a⟩|.
(ii) For each σ, Cauchy–Schwarz |⟨u_{σ(a)}, w_a⟩| ≤ ‖u_{σ(a)}‖·‖w_a‖ (abs_real_inner_le_norm) and monotonicity of products of nonnegative reals give Π_a |⟨u_{σ(a)}, w_a⟩| ≤ Π_a (‖u_{σ(a)}‖·‖w_a‖) = (Π_a ‖u_{σ(a)}‖)·(Π_a ‖w_a‖).
(iii) Since σ is a bijection of Fin n, reindexing gives Π_a ‖u_{σ(a)}‖ = Π_a ‖u_a‖ (Equiv.prod_comp).
(iv) There are n! permutations of Fin n (Fintype.card_perm). Summing the constant bound from (ii)–(iii) over σ gives |β⁰(u)| ≤ n!·(Π_b ‖w_b‖)·(Π_a ‖u_a‖) = C·Π_a ‖u_a‖, where C := n!·Π_b ‖w_b‖ does not depend on u.

4. Continuity and conclusion. AlternatingMap.mkContinuous f C H turns an alternating n-linear map f with ‖f(u)‖ ≤ C·Π_a ‖u_a‖ for all u into a continuous alternating map with the same values. Let β := β⁰.mkContinuous C H, with H the bound of step 3. Then β is a continuous alternating n-linear form, i.e. β ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n. For every u, β(u) = β⁰(u) = det(⟨u_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} by step 2. So β witnesses the existential. ∎
proof_key_steps: The row map p_w(x) := (⟨x, w_b⟩)_b is ℝ-linear because the inner product is linear in its first argument.
β⁰ := Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap p_w is alternating n-linear, and β⁰(u) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => ⟨u_a, w_b⟩) by unfolding the definitions.
The Leibniz formula, |sgn σ| = 1, Cauchy–Schwarz, reindexing along σ and n! permutations give |β⁰(u)| ≤ (n!·Π_b‖w_b‖)·Π_a‖u_a‖.
β := β⁰.mkContinuous (n!·Π_b‖w_b‖) is a Covector (Euclid P) n with the same values as β⁰, so it witnesses the claim.

subproblems.title: Equal mixed determinants against every frame force span inclusion of orthonormal frames
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let x = (x_1, …, x_n) and y = (y_1, …, y_n) be orthonormal families in ℝ^P (Orthonormal ℝ x, Orthonormal ℝ y). Assume that for every family w = (w_1, …, w_n) of vectors in ℝ^P (w : Fin n → Euclid P), det(⟨x_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} = det(⟨y_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b}. Here (⟨u_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} is the n×n real matrix with entry ⟨u_a, w_b⟩ in row a and column b (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (u a) (w b)). Then span{y_1, …, y_n} ⊆ span{x_1, …, x_n}, i.e. Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range y) ≤ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x y : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ x → Orthonormal ℝ y → (∀ w : Fin n → Euclid P, Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (x a) (w b)) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun a b => inner ℝ (y a) (w b))) → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range y) ≤ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product on ℝ^P; it is real, hence symmetric. ‖·‖ is its norm and δ_{ab} the Kronecker delta. For u, w ∈ (ℝ^P)^n write G(u, w) := (⟨u_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} = Matrix.of fun a b => ⟨u_a, w_b⟩, with row index a and column index b. Orthonormality of x and y means ⟨x_a, x_j⟩ = δ_{aj} and ⟨y_a, y_b⟩ = δ_{ab} for all indices (orthonormal_iff_ite). The hypothesis says det G(x, w) = det G(y, w) for every w.

1. Reduction. By Submodule.span_le it suffices to show range y ⊆ span x, i.e. y_i ∈ span x for every index i. If n = 0 there is no index and the claim is immediate. Fix i.

2. Orthogonal residual. Put c_j := ⟨x_j, y_i⟩ for each j and e := y_i − Σ_j c_j·x_j. Fix any index a. The inner product is linear in its second argument and x is orthonormal, so ⟨x_a, e⟩ = ⟨x_a, y_i⟩ − Σ_j c_j·⟨x_a, x_j⟩ = ⟨x_a, y_i⟩ − Σ_j c_j·δ_{aj}. Only the term j = a survives the sum, so this equals ⟨x_a, y_i⟩ − c_a. By symmetry of the real inner product c_a = ⟨x_a, y_i⟩, hence ⟨x_a, e⟩ = 0.

3. Test frame. Let w := Function.update y i e, so that w_i = e and w_b = y_b for every b ≠ i.
(a) The column of G(x, w) with index i is (⟨x_a, w_i⟩)_a = (⟨x_a, e⟩)_a, which is 0 by step 2. A square matrix with a zero column has determinant 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_column_eq_zero). Hence det G(x, w) = 0.
(b) Let d := (⟨y_a, e⟩)_a ∈ ℝ^n.
  - For b ≠ i: G(y, w)_{ab} = ⟨y_a, y_b⟩ = δ_{ab}, the (a, b) entry of the identity matrix 1.
  - For b = i: G(y, w)_{ai} = ⟨y_a, e⟩ = d_a.
  - By Matrix.updateCol_apply, (1.updateCol i d)_{ab} = d_a if b = i and 1_{ab} otherwise. Hence G(y, w) = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).updateCol i d.
  - By Cramer's rule, det(A.updateCol i d) = (cramer A d)_i (Matrix.cramer_apply), and cramer of the identity matrix is the identity map (Matrix.cramer_one).
  - Therefore det G(y, w) = (cramer 1 d)_i = d_i = ⟨y_i, e⟩.
  Equivalently: for every a ≠ i, subtracting d_a times column a from column i leaves the determinant unchanged. The result is the diagonal matrix with diagonal 1, …, d_i, …, 1, whose determinant is d_i.
(c) The hypothesis for this w gives ⟨y_i, e⟩ = det G(y, w) = det G(x, w) = 0 by (a) and (b).

4. The residual vanishes. Expand e = y_i − Σ_j c_j·x_j in the first slot: ⟨e, e⟩ = ⟨y_i, e⟩ − Σ_j c_j·⟨x_j, e⟩. By step 3(c) and step 2 this is 0 − Σ_j c_j·0 = 0. Since ⟨e, e⟩ = ‖e‖² = 0, we get e = 0 (inner_self_eq_zero), i.e. y_i = Σ_j c_j·x_j.

5. Conclusion. Each x_j lies in span x (Submodule.subset_span). Hence so does c_j·x_j (Submodule.smul_mem), and so does the finite sum Σ_j c_j·x_j (Submodule.sum_mem). By step 4, y_i ∈ span x. Since i was arbitrary, range y ⊆ span x, and step 1 gives span y ⊆ span x. ∎
proof_key_steps: By Submodule.span_le it suffices to show y_i ∈ span x for each index i.
The residual e := y_i − Σ_j ⟨x_j, y_i⟩ x_j satisfies ⟨x_a, e⟩ = 0 for every a, by orthonormality of x.
Take w := Function.update y i e. G(x, w) has zero column i, so its determinant is 0. G(y, w) = (1 : Matrix).updateCol i (⟨y_a, e⟩)_a, so its determinant is ⟨y_i, e⟩ by cramer_apply and cramer_one.
The hypothesis gives ⟨y_i, e⟩ = 0. Then ⟨e, e⟩ = ⟨y_i, e⟩ − Σ_j ⟨x_j, y_i⟩⟨x_j, e⟩ = 0, so e = 0 and y_i = Σ_j ⟨x_j, y_i⟩ x_j ∈ span x.

subproblems.title: Subsequence criterion for an approximate tangent plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P, a ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim Q = n (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n). Write Hⁿ = μHE[n] and blowUpMap a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a). Assume: for every sequence (λ_i)_{i∈ℕ} with λ_i > 0 for all i and λ_i → 0, there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that, for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{blowUpMap a λ_{φ(k)} '' M} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as k → ∞. Then M has approximate tangent space Q at a, i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a Q: finrank Q = n and ∫_{blowUpMap a r '' M} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0) for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (a : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → (∀ lams : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < lams i) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a (lams (φ k)) '' M, f y ∂μHE[n]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ y in (Q : Set (Euclid P)), f y ∂μHE[n]))) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n]; for r ∈ ℝ, N_r := blowUpMap a r '' M, where blowUpMap a r y = r⁻¹(y − a).

1. By definition (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a Q means: finrank Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), F(r) := ∫_{N_r} f dHⁿ tends to L := ∫_Q f dHⁿ along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. The first part is the hypothesis finrank Q = n. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ); as a function ℝ^P → ℝ it is continuous and has compact support.

2. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is countably generated. By the subsequence criterion (Filter.tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto) it suffices to show: for every sequence r : ℕ → ℝ with r_j → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, there is ψ : ℕ → ℕ with F(r_{ψ(k)}) → L as k → ∞.

3. Let such a sequence r be given.
 - Since (0, ∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0, eventually r_j ∈ (0, ∞): there is j₀ with r_j > 0 for all j ≥ j₀ (Filter.eventually_atTop).
 - Since 𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0, r_j → 0 in ℝ (tendsto_nhds_of_tendsto_nhdsWithin).

4. Define λ_i := r_{i+j₀}. Then λ_i > 0 for every i, because i + j₀ ≥ j₀. Also λ_i → 0, because a shifted sequence has the same limit (tendsto_add_atTop_iff_nat). By the hypothesis there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with ∫_{N_{λ_{φ(k)}}} g dHⁿ → ∫_Q g dHⁿ for every continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → ℝ. Apply this to g := f.

5. Put ψ(k) := φ(k) + j₀. Then r_{ψ(k)} = λ_{φ(k)}, so F(r_{ψ(k)}) = ∫_{N_{λ_{φ(k)}}} f dHⁿ → L. This verifies the criterion of step 2, so F(r) → L along 𝓝[>] 0. Since f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) was arbitrary, together with finrank Q = n this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M a Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt: finrank Q = n is given; for each f ∈ C_c show F(r) = ∫_{blowUpMap a r '' M} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0.
Use the subsequence criterion Filter.tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto; 𝓝[>] 0 is countably generated.
A sequence r_j → 0⁺ is positive from some j₀ on and tends to 0; apply the hypothesis to λ_i = r_{i+j₀} and take ψ(k) = φ(k) + j₀.

subproblems.title: Lower density of the weight of a constant-orientation cycle with the integer slice property
subproblems.statement:
Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, B_r(x) = ball x r; densities are in [0, ∞] with ofReal.
An admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) consists of a Borel measure μ finite on compact sets and a μ-a.e. strongly measurable field ξ of k-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for all test k-forms ω.
Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) has the integer slice property (ISP) if the following holds for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ: for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity.
Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d + 1, η₀, θ₀ ∈ ℝ, ν a Borel measure on ℝ^P, ζ₀ an n-vector (MultiVector P n) and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P).
Assume (LD_{η₀}): let C' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂C' = 0, μ a Borel measure finite on compact sets with M_W(C') = μ(W) for all open W, and ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and C'(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for all test n-forms ω. If C' has ISP, then ofReal η₀ ≤ liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) for μ-a.e. x.
Assume moreover: θ₀ > 0; ∂C = 0; ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K; M_W(C) = ofReal(θ₀)·ν(W) for every open W; |ζ₀(β)| ≤ |β| for every n-covector β; C(ω) = ∫θ₀ζ₀(ω(y))dν(y) for every test n-form ω; and C has ISP.
Then ofReal(η₀/θ₀) ≤ liminf_{r↓0} ν(B_r(y))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) for ν-a.e. y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (η₀ θ₀ : ℝ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (ζ₀ : MultiVector P (d + 1)) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)), (∀ (C' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (d + 1)), C'.boundary = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → C'.massOn W = μ W) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), C' ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (d + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P d), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ' K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' μ' → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ', ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) d, |ξ' x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), C' ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, (C').boundary η = ∫ x, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ') → ∀ (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzWith L f → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), A ω = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, B η = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ') → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A.boundary - B)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ENNReal.ofReal η₀ ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => μ (ball x r) / (unitBallVolume (d + 1) * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (d + 1)))) (𝓝[>] 0)) → 0 < θ₀ → C.boundary = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → C.massOn W = ENNReal.ofReal θ₀ * ν W) → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), |ζ₀ β| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm β) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), C ω = ∫ y, θ₀ * ζ₀ ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) y) ∂ν) → (∀ (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (d + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P d), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ' K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' μ' → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (d + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ', ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) d, |ξ' x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), C ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, (C).boundary η = ∫ x, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ') → ∀ (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), LipschitzWith L f → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1), A ω = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (d + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, B η = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) x) ∂μ') → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A.boundary - B)) → ∀ᵐ y ∂ν, ENNReal.ofReal (η₀ / θ₀) ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => ν (ball y r) / (unitBallVolume (d + 1) * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ (d + 1)))) (𝓝[>] 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: n = d + 1, B_r(x) = ball x r, D(r) := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ) with ω_n = unitBallVolume n; all quantities below are in [0, ∞].

1. Put c := ofReal θ₀. Since θ₀ > 0: c ≠ 0, c ≠ ∞ and c.toReal = θ₀. Let μ' := c • ν, so μ'(S) = c·ν(S) (Measure.smul_apply). Let ξ be the constant field ξ(x) := ζ₀.

2. Apply the hypothesis LD_{η₀} to C' := C, μ := μ' and this ξ. Its hypotheses hold:
 (a) ∂C = 0 by hypothesis.
 (b) For compact K, μ'(K) = c·ν(K) < ∞, because c < ∞ and ν(K) < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
 (c) For open W, M_W(C) = ofReal(θ₀)·ν(W) = μ'(W), by the mass hypothesis and Measure.smul_apply.
 (d) ξ is constant, hence μ'-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_const).
 (e) |ξ(x)(α)| = |ζ₀(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α, in particular μ'-a.e.
 (f) For every test n-form ω: ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ'(x) = c.toReal·∫ζ₀(ω(x))dν(x) (integral_smul_measure) = θ₀·∫ζ₀(ω(x))dν(x) = ∫θ₀ζ₀(ω(x))dν(x) (integral_const_mul) = C(ω), by the representation hypothesis.
 (g) C has ISP by hypothesis. This is exactly the ISP premise of LD_{η₀} for C' = C.
 Hence, for μ'-a.e. x: ofReal η₀ ≤ liminf_{r→0⁺} μ'(B_r(x))/D(r).

3. Since c ≠ 0, ν ≪ μ' = c • ν (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_smul). So the conclusion of step 2 holds for ν-a.e. x. Fix such an x.

4. For every r, μ'(B_r(x))/D(r) = (c·ν(B_r(x)))/D(r) = c·(ν(B_r(x))/D(r)), by Measure.smul_apply and mul_div_assoc in [0, ∞]. Let g(r) := ν(B_r(x))/D(r) and ℓ := liminf_{r→0⁺} g(r). Since c ≠ ∞ and 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter, liminf_{r→0⁺} c·g(r) = c·ℓ (ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top). Step 2 therefore gives ofReal η₀ ≤ c·ℓ.

5. ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos needs only θ₀ > 0 and holds for every real η₀ (if η₀ ≤ 0 both sides are 0), so ofReal(η₀/θ₀) = ofReal η₀ / ofReal θ₀ = ofReal η₀ / c. By step 4, ofReal η₀ ≤ c·ℓ, hence ofReal η₀ / c ≤ ℓ (ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul'). Therefore ofReal(η₀/θ₀) ≤ ℓ = liminf_{r→0⁺} ν(B_r(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)). This holds for ν-a.e. x, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Apply LD_{η₀} to C with the measure ofReal θ₀ • ν and the constant field ζ₀: finite on compacts, mass identity via Measure.smul_apply, representation via integral_smul_measure and integral_const_mul, and the ISP of C.
Transfer the a.e. statement from ofReal θ₀ • ν to ν (ν ≪ c • ν since c ≠ 0).

Rewrite (c·ν(B))/D = c·(ν(B)/D), pull the finite constant c out of the liminf (ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top), and conclude ofReal(η₀/θ₀) = ofReal η₀ / c ≤ ℓ by ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos and ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul'.

subproblems.title: Weights at least one with total at most one force a single plane through the origin
subproblems.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, m and ν measures on ℝ^P, V a linear subspace of ℝ^P, w_1, …, w_N ∈ ℝ^P and α_1, …, α_N ∈ ℝ (indices in Fin N). Assume α_i ≥ 1 for every i, Σ_iα_i ≤ 1, w_{i₀} = 0 for some i₀, and ν = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·(m⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V}). Then ν = m⌞V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (m ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (w : Fin N → Euclid P) (α : Fin N → ℝ), (∀ i, 1 ≤ α i) → ∑ i, α i ≤ 1 → (∃ i, w i = 0) → ν = ∑ i, ENNReal.ofReal (α i) • m.restrict {y : Euclid P | y - w i ∈ V} → ν = m.restrict (V : Set (Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. By hypothesis choose an index i₀ with w_{i₀} = 0.

2. Every index equals i₀. Suppose i ≠ i₀. All α_j ≥ 1 ≥ 0, so the sum over the two-element set {i, i₀} is at most the sum over all indices (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg). That two-element sum equals α_i + α_{i₀} (Finset.sum_pair). Hence α_i + α_{i₀} ≤ Σ_jα_j ≤ 1. But α_i + α_{i₀} ≥ 1 + 1 = 2, a contradiction.

3. By step 2, every sum over the index set equals its i₀-term (Finset.sum_eq_single i₀; all other terms are indexed by some j ≠ i₀, which cannot exist). In particular Σ_jα_j = α_{i₀}, so α_{i₀} ≤ 1. Together with α_{i₀} ≥ 1 this gives α_{i₀} = 1.

4. Likewise ν = Σ_i ofReal(α_i)·(m⌞{y : y − w_i ∈ V}) = ofReal(α_{i₀})·(m⌞{y : y − w_{i₀} ∈ V}) = ofReal(1)·(m⌞{y : y − 0 ∈ V}). Since ofReal 1 = 1, one_smul and y − 0 = y, this equals m⌞{y : y ∈ V} = m⌞V, where {y : y ∈ V} is the carrier set (V : Set ℝ^P). ∎
proof_key_steps: Pick i₀ with w_{i₀} = 0; two distinct indices would give Σα ≥ α_i + α_{i₀} ≥ 2 > 1, so every index is i₀.
Then Σα = α_{i₀}, so α_{i₀} = 1, and the sum of measures collapses to ofReal(1)·m⌞{y : y − 0 ∈ V} = m⌞V.
